newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two bombs explode in Corsica, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs explode in Corsica, no casualties.

text.p: Two bombs exploded on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, causing damage but no casualties, police said on Friday.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the attacks which took place late on Thursday night in the northern port of Bastia.
One bomb went off outside a bar, damaging the establishment and parked cars nearby while the second exploded in an office in the city's industrial zone, police said.

There was no immediate indication if the attacks were by suspected separatist guerrillas, who have been waging a low-level bombing campaign for two decades for more autonomy from mainland France, or by local gangsters.
Police say it is difficult to distinguish between the two since they believe the same men are often involved.
